text.p: Following are the highlights of main stories in Serbian and Montenegrin papers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
POLITIKA
- Serbian parliament to hold session on August 19 to elect a committe for supervision of September 21 elections.
- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic said on his return from a two-day visit to Athens that most progress in Yugoslav-Greek relations was marked in the sphere of economy.
- A sum of 946 million German marks remains frozen in the off-shore office of Beogradska Banka AD in Cyprus following a suit filed by Slovenia.
- Yugoslavia to boost trade with Egypt following visit of a Yugoslav delegation to that country. Yugoslavia's export chance are cars, tractors, tyres, railway carriages and tourism.
- Raising of the reserve requirement to 20 from 15 percent by the central bank followed an abrupt increase of banks' liquidity.

- Majdanpek gold mine called the state to prevent smuggling of gold jewelry which has taken on "enormous proportions", costing state coffers 80 million German marks a year and threatening domestic production.
- Serbia is to complete a road reconstruction programme worth 816.2 million dinars this year.
- Vojvodina province plans to construct 16 new telephone exchanges by end of year.
- Serbian government headed by Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic will hold a session in Pristina to discuss regional development policy.
- Weather is favourable for sugarbeet but more sunny days would be good for other crops.
- Complete reform of the legislative system is being prepared, said Serbian Deputy Justice Minister Nebojsa Sarkic.
- Politika calls second meeting of its shareholders on September 7.
- Election slogan of the opposition Democratic Party of Serbia (DSS) will be "Boycott - My Choice" and of the Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) "For Serbia".
- The opposition Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO) has decided to freeze all activities until fulfilment of its conditions for election participation.
- Californian company ICN Pharmaceuticals, which also has its affilate in Belgrade and is headed by Serbian-born businessman Milan Panic, plans to expand in Eastern Europe.
- Farm cooperatives and state agricultural firms in Serbia ask for postponement of credit repayment until end of year.
- Supporters of the Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO) threw eggs at Zoran Djindjic, the leader of the Democratic Party (DS) and former SPO coalition partner during a rally in Kraljevo, Serbia.
BORBA

- Federal Justice Minister Zoran Knezevic said the breakaway faction of the Democratic Party of Socialists of Montenegro belongs to the noveau-riche and said he was opposed to the constitutional court annulling Momir Bulatovic's presidential candidacy.
- Zastava cars expected to announce its foreign partner by end of August, unnamed sources said.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Kragujevac cars will produce 2,000 units this month, 960 of which are for exports to Egypt and 500 to Poland.
- There is no need for OSCE or other international organisations to monitor Serbia's elections, said Aleksandar Vulin, the vice-president of the Yugoslav Left (JUL), a ruling coalition partner.
- The Serbian Unity Party (SSJ), headed by Zeljko Raznatovic "Arkan", will participate in the Serbian elections in Kosovo district.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA

- The Montenegrin Constitutional court publicly discussed the Democratic Party of Socialists appeal on the Republican Election Commission decision to approve Momir Bulatovic as the DPS presidential candidate for next elections.
- The authorities prevented several hundered Albanian tourists from spending their holidays in Ulcinj because they did not have visas.

- Companies complain it is very difficult to get bank credits. Montenegro-based banks granted only 413 million dinars of credits to the republic's economy this year while non-Montenegro banks loaned 73 million dinars. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
